newsitem.title: UK: Nelson Gold sets eyes on Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Nelson Gold sets eyes on Kazakhstan.

text.p: Mining minnow Nelson Gold Corp Ltd, the biggest foreign investor in Tajikistan, on Friday outlined a plan to catapult itself into a league of bigger players by 2005.
Founded in 1994, Nelson Gold has started looking for projects in Kazakhstan and aims to boost production at its main Tajik operation by nearly eight times in coming years.
"In five to 10 years from now we can see ourselves as a medium-sized player," president and chief executive officer Glenn Laing said at a company presentation here.
Nelson Gold has already opened a reprensentative office in Almaty in Kazakhstan and "we can see one or two projects coming our way," Laing said.
London-based and Toronto-listed Nelson Gold is operator of the open-cast Jilau mine in the north west of former Soviet republic Tajikistan.
It operates the mine through its 44 percent stake in the Zeravashan Gold Company, a joint venture with the Tajik government.
Gold exports from Jilau, which started in December, will generate the cash flow which will be the main source for funding Nelson Gold's ambitions in Central Asia.
Laing said his company did not plan to tap capital markets to finance the expansion of the Jilau mine. Neither did he see any necessity in the near future to team-up with a major mining firm.
Attributable production from Jilau was 16,000 ounces in 1996 and is scheduled to climb to 32,000 this year to eventually reach about 125,000 ounces by 2000.
Attributable production was about 10,000 ounces below company forecasts last year as it took the Tajik government more time to implement financial and export agreements than Nelson Gold had expected.
"It is a transitional economy in a transitional country, so there are many chances and demands on the government," said Laing.
"With hindsight we can say...we underestimated the difficulties the government had in implementing the agreements it had with us," he added.
